name: CI-SPEED-AND-RELIABILITY

requirements_confirmation.selected_option: Accept these requirements and create the roadmap.

phases.name: Measure Current CI
phases.goal: Contributors and maintainers can identify today's CI waiting time, failure patterns, and largest runtime costs before choosing fixes.
criteria: A current report separates pull-request, main-push, and nightly runs and shows waiting time, execution time, literal conclusions, and rerun attempts with their saved source data.
Measured job, step, and test costs identify the largest setup/cache/execution costs; current failure signatures form a concrete, bounded flaky-test shortlist.
The baseline and ranked findings can be reproduced with documented commands using the saved inputs; static timeout values or old audit conclusions are not used as runtime measurements.

Before any optimization, the report fixes the comparison workloads, code revisions, cache conditions, runner class, sample sizes, percentile method, and finite collection/rate-limit budget. The 20% median improvement and non-increasing p95/runner-time targets stay unchanged.

phases.name: Fix Flaky CI and Preserve Required Checks
phases.goal: Selected flaky CI failures are reproducible and fixed, while real failures still prevent the required checks from passing.
criteria: Each selected current flaky failure has a deterministic reproduction, a root-cause fix in the test or CI harness, and passing regression/repeat checks under the fixed budget. If the baseline found no flake, that result and repeated isolation/readiness checks are recorded without inventing a bug.
Browser/test retries are not increased and readiness is asserted without sleeps; tests continue to use isolated application/database state where needed.
Required-check names and useful test ownership remain intact. Any accepted removal of a redundant check includes a comparison showing its useful coverage still executes.
Injected failures, cancellations, missing expected jobs, and unexpected skips prevent a green required gate; documented intentional skips remain distinguishable from missing execution.

phases.name: Speed Up the Measured Slow Jobs
phases.goal: Contributors receive the required PR CI result at least 20% sooner without increasing slow-run waits or total runner time.
criteria: The recorded optimization targets the measured costs from Phase 252 and is tested on the same predeclared workloads, runner class, and cache conditions.
Saved real before/after run data show required PR-result median elapsed time at or below 80% of the baseline, calculated by the fixed method.
The same comparison shows a 95th-percentile required-result wait no higher than baseline and total runner time per comparable PR no higher than baseline.

The changed CI paths still pass the Phase 253 coverage/gate checks and applicable isolation/cache tests. A target miss is recorded as a miss; the collection window is not extended until the numbers look favorable.

phases.name: Make Failures Reproducible and Report the Result
phases.goal: Contributors can reproduce updated CI checks locally and maintainers can independently replay the final speed and reliability comparison.
criteria: Documented local commands execute the relevant updated CI paths, with mix ci retained as the contributor entry point and any browser/database preparation made explicit.
A deliberately failed updated check identifies the failed test or command, reproduction command and applicable seed, and retained logs/traces needed to diagnose it.
A documented calculation replays the final before/after comparison from saved inputs, including sample sizes, literal failure/cancellation/rerun outcomes, cache conditions, and limitations.

The final report names the tested code, states whether the 20% median and non-increasing p95/runner-time targets hold, and records any remaining failures separately from implemented changes. Missing old release approvals or signed historical performance archives are not required inputs.
